findings.issue_text: Duplicate method definition of `def self.downsize` in app/models/optimized_image.rb — Ruby doesn't support overloading, so the second definition replaces the first, breaking existing callers with the old arity
In-place convert reads and writes the same file in uploads_controller.rb — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` can truncate/corrupt the source before it's fully read
Downsize loop gives up silently after 5 attempts and proceeds with an oversized image, providing no user feedback that downsizing failed

Client-side file size limit hardcoded to 10MB in utilities.js ignores the site's max_image_size_kb setting, causing mismatched error messages and wrong blocking; same for the 10.megabytes download cap in FileHelper.download in uploads_controller.rb

Downsizing condition relies on `filename` extension via FileHelper.is_image?(filename) instead of content_type/fastimage detection, so URL-sourced images without recognizable extensions skip downsizing and misnamed non-images get converted

`allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` semantics misuse — the setting governs thumbnails, but is used to flatten the user's original animated GIF during upload reduction, destroying the original animation (data loss)
`tempfile.size > 0` guard is ineffective as an image check — non-image files with image-looking names pass into the ImageMagick convert loop without content validation

Duplicate `downsize` method definition in optimized_image.rb: second definition silently overrides the original, causing old 4-arg callers to bind max_height into dimensions and produce garbage geometry like "100x-"

In-place `convert` on the same input/output path in uploads_controller.rb: passing the same file as `from` and `to` risks a truncated/corrupt file on failed/interrupted convert; should downsize to a new tempfile
Downsize loop may never reach target size: 5 iterations at 80% only reduce to ~33% of pixels, so large images can exit the loop still over the limit and be rejected anyway, wasting CPU
Repeated synchronous full re-encodes of large images on the request thread block a web worker for potentially seconds per upload, a DoS-ish cost for busy servers
Hard-coded 10MB client/server caps replace tunable SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, letting client allow files the server rejects and increasing download resource use for sites with small limits

allow_animation only honored for .GIF extension, but tempfile paths have no extension so animated images fall to the single-frame path, making repeated 80% re-encodes of large animated GIFs extremely expensive
No client-side pre-downsize: large image is fully uploaded before server-side reduction, costing the user full upload bandwidth; canvas-based client downsizing would avoid the transfer
Duplicate self.downsize method definition in optimized_image.rb: last definition wins, making the 4-positional-arg version dead code and breaking existing callers with ArgumentError
Downsize result (false return on ImageMagick failure) is ignored by uploads_controller; in-place write on same input tempfile can corrupt the upload which is still passed to Upload.create_for
Retry loop can exhaust 5 attempts and still upload an oversized file, with no logging or exception handling around the downsize call
Hardcoded client-side 10MB limit in utilities.js diverges from SiteSettings max size KB, causing both missed client-side rejections and incorrect rejections, plus misleading error message in KB units
Five synchronous ImageMagick invocations in the request path with no timeout, creating a resource-exhaustion vector; '80%' quality reduction is unpredictable for already-compressed images
FileHelper.download size cap hardcoded to 10MB in uploads_controller, inconsistent with site settings for max_image_size_kb

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place convert reads and writes the same file in uploads_controller.rb — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` can truncate/corrupt the source before it's fully read

adjudication.rationale: The new loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, passing the same path as both source and destination. In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize/optimize` ultimately runs an external convert command via `convert_with(instructions, to)` with no temp-file/rename safety in the shown diff, so in-place read/write can fail or corrupt/truncate the file depending on the underlying tool behavior. This is a correctness/data-loss risk introduced by the added downsize loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize loop gives up silently after 5 attempts and proceeds with an oversized image, providing no user feedback that downsizing failed

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing logic (`attempt = 5` loop calling `OptimizedImage.downsize` while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) has no post-loop check and no error/alert/log if the file is still oversized; execution always proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)`. The claim that an oversized image will definitely be accepted isn’t provable from this diff (depends on `Upload.create_for` validations), but the “gives up silently after 5 attempts with no user feedback” concern is directly supported by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side file size limit hardcoded to 10MB in utilities.js ignores the site's max_image_size_kb setting, causing mismatched error messages and wrong blocking; same for the 10.megabytes download cap in FileHelper.download in uploads_controller.rb

Downsizing condition relies on `filename` extension via FileHelper.is_image?(filename) instead of content_type/fastimage detection, so URL-sourced images without recognizable extensions skip downsizing and misnamed non-images get converted

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing block in `uploads_controller.rb` gates resizing on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` (using only `filename`, even for URL-sourced uploads where `filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`). The diff does not show any content-type or actual-bytes image detection being used for this decision. That makes the new “auto-reduce large images” behavior potentially incomplete for cases where the URL path/filename is not indicative of image-ness (e.g., missing/odd extension) and could also attempt downsizing based on a misleading filename. This is a concrete edge-case/scope issue introduced by the change, but the exact behavior of `is_image?` isn’t shown in the diff, so it’s not fully verifiable as a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` semantics misuse — the setting governs thumbnails, but is used to flatten the user's original animated GIF during upload reduction, destroying the original animation (data loss)

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, large images are downsized in-place (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`). In `optimized_image.rb`, `allow_animation` controls whether the `_animated` instruction path is used for `.GIF` files. If `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, downsizing a large animated GIF will take the non-animated path and can drop animation frames while overwriting the original upload tempfile, causing irreversible data loss. The setting name also suggests it is scoped to thumbnails, not original uploads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `tempfile.size > 0` guard is ineffective as an image check — non-image files with image-looking names pass into the ImageMagick convert loop without content validation

adjudication.rationale: The new pre-upload downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` runs when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true, which (as shown) is based on the `filename` rather than validated file content. That means a non-image payload with an image-looking name/extension can enter the `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` ImageMagick/convert loop. The `tempfile.size > 0` check only ensures non-empty data and does not prevent this. This is a real behavior change introduced by the diff and can lead to erroneous processing or security risk from invoking ImageMagick on untrusted non-image input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate `downsize` method definition in optimized_image.rb: second definition silently overrides the original, causing old 4-arg callers to bind max_height into dimensions and produce garbage geometry like "100x-"

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, the diff leaves two `def self.downsize` definitions: one taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and a later one taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not overload methods, so the second definition silently replaces the first. Any existing 4-arg callers will now be dispatched to the 3-required-arg version, misbinding arguments (e.g., `opts` becoming `max_height`) and likely causing incorrect geometry or runtime errors when `optimize` accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place `convert` on the same input/output path in uploads_controller.rb: passing the same file as `from` and `to` risks a truncated/corrupt file on failed/interrupted convert; should downsize to a new tempfile

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, explicitly using the same path for input (`from`) and output (`to`). Given `OptimizedImage#convert_with` shells out to an external `convert`-style command to write `to`, in-place conversion can corrupt/truncate the tempfile if the convert process fails or is interrupted, and subsequent retries would operate on an already-damaged file. This is a real data-loss/correctness risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize loop may never reach target size: 5 iterations at 80% only reduce to ~33% of pixels, so large images can exit the loop still over the limit and be rejected anyway, wasting CPU

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that repeatedly downsizes an oversized image up to 5 times using a fixed `"80%"` factor (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes ... OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`). From the diff alone it’s clear this is a best-effort attempt with a hard stop, so an image can still remain over the configured limit after 5 iterations and then proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` (likely to be rejected), meaning extra CPU work may be wasted. The specific numeric claim about reaching only ~33% of pixels isn’t verifiable here, but the general concern (fixed iterations/factor may not achieve target size) is grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Repeated synchronous full re-encodes of large images on the request thread block a web worker for potentially seconds per upload, a DoS-ish cost for busy servers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds synchronous image recompression in `UploadsController#create_upload`: a `while` loop (up to 5 iterations) calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` while the tempfile is larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately shells out to ImageMagick via `convert_with` (backticks). This work happens on the request thread before `Upload.create_for`, so large images can trigger multiple full re-encodes and block a web worker for a noticeable time, creating a plausible DoS/performance risk on busy servers. This is a real review concern grounded in the change, but not necessarily a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hard-coded 10MB client/server caps replace tunable SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, letting client allow files the server rejects and increasing download resource use for sites with small limits
matched_golden_ids: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core problem: a hard-coded 10MB/10*1024KB limit on the client (and implied handling) that ignores the configurable Discourse SiteSetting max_*_size_kb, leading to divergence between client-side validation and server-side/per-site limits. The candidate is less specific about per-type settings and the 413 handler, but matches the underlying issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: allow_animation only honored for .GIF extension, but tempfile paths have no extension so animated images fall to the single-frame path, making repeated 80% re-encodes of large animated GIFs extremely expensive

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated path is only chosen when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Since `from` is `tempfile.path` (and for URL downloads the temp name is `"discourse-upload-#{type}"` with no extension), this regex will typically fail even for GIF uploads, so animated GIFs will be processed by the non-animated instructions (likely flattening to a single frame) and repeatedly re-encoded in the `while` loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No client-side pre-downsize: large image is fully uploaded before server-side reduction, costing the user full upload bandwidth; canvas-based client downsizing would avoid the transfer

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds server-side downsizing in `UploadsController#create_upload` (loop calling `OptimizedImage.downsize` when the uploaded tempfile exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`), but does not add any client-side resizing. The client-side code in `utilities.js` only enforces a fixed 10MB limit (`var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`) and still uploads the full file before any reduction can occur. The finding is therefore a valid performance/UX concern (bandwidth/time), not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate self.downsize method definition in optimized_image.rb: last definition wins, making the 4-positional-arg version dead code and breaking existing callers with ArgumentError

adjudication.rationale: In optimized_image.rb the diff leaves an existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` later. In Ruby the later definition overrides the earlier one, so the 4-positional-arg API becomes dead code and any existing callers passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` will hit the new signature and raise `ArgumentError` for wrong number of arguments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize result (false return on ImageMagick failure) is ignored by uploads_controller; in-place write on same input tempfile can corrupt the upload which is still passed to Upload.create_for

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb` the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e. it writes output to the same path as the input tempfile. Any failure/corruption from this in-place ImageMagick operation would still lead to `Upload.create_for(...)` using that tempfile. Additionally, `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` on nonzero exit status (and `nil` otherwise), but the controller ignores the return value entirely, so it cannot detect/stop on failed downsizing before uploading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retry loop can exhaust 5 attempts and still upload an oversized file, with no logging or exception handling around the downsize call

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop downsizes at most 5 times (`attempt = 5` ... `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`), but after it finishes there is no final check that `tempfile.size` is now within `max_image_size_kb` before calling `Upload.create_for(...)`. Also, `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` has a failure signal (`convert_with` returns `false` when the command exit status is non-zero), but the controller ignores that return value and has no logging/handling around the downsize attempts. Whether an oversized file is ultimately accepted depends on validations in `Upload.create_for`, which are not shown in the diff, so the “still upload” part isn’t fully verifiable here, but the lack of post-condition check/handling is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded client-side 10MB limit in utilities.js diverges from SiteSettings max size KB, causing both missed client-side rejections and incorrect rejections, plus misleading error message in KB units

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the upload size limit is changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in two places. This clearly diverges from server-configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (still used in `uploads_controller.rb` for downsizing), so client-side acceptance/rejection can become inconsistent with the actual configured limits. The error message will also always report `10240` KB regardless of the SiteSetting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Five synchronous ImageMagick invocations in the request path with no timeout, creating a resource-exhaustion vector; '80%' quality reduction is unpredictable for already-compressed images

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times synchronously in the request path when an uploaded image exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. `OptimizedImage` ultimately runs ImageMagick via backticks in `convert_with` with no timeout or resource limiting shown, so repeated conversions can be used to tie up server CPU/memory (DoS/resource exhaustion). The note about using a fixed "80%" quality string is also grounded (`OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`) and can behave unpredictably for already-compressed images, but the no-timeout repeated invocations are the clearest defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FileHelper.download size cap hardcoded to 10MB in uploads_controller, inconsistent with site settings for max_image_size_kb

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb#create_upload`, the URL-download cap is changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. This makes API URL uploads ignore `max_image_size_kb` and can incorrectly reject downloads when the site setting allows >10MB (or allow larger-than-configured downloads when the setting is <10MB), creating inconsistent and potentially broken behavior relative to configuration.
